evidence.api_compatibility: No API changes. The only surface is the build system: the old code used bare `target_link_libraries(... PRIVATE drm_amdgpu)`, and the new code uses pkg-config to resolve the same library within an `if(PkgConfig_FOUND)` block. This does not change the compiled binary's ABI, exported symbols, CLI, or any user-facing API. A build-time dependency on pkg-config is implied, but pkg-config is ubiquitous on modern Linux and was already used in the same file for libcap.
evidence.documentation: No documentation changes needed. The author checked 'Documentation is not affected by this change' in the PR template. This is a build-system internal improvement that does not alter user-facing behavior, CLI options, or configuration.
evidence.manual_release_testing: Not required. The change is build-system-only (CMakeLists.txt) and does not introduce user-facing behavior — it only changes how the build finds libdrm_amdgpu include/library paths. CI already exercises the full Linux build pipeline on amd64 and arm64, and the author confirmed on-target testing with actual AMD hardware.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None. The PR contained a single commit (3dd5379). The PR was merged with that same commit as the merge commit (a5dbbb1). There are zero commits added after approval, so no post-approval drift to assess.
evidence.review: PR #3516 was approved by @superm1 (MEMBER) at 2026-09-09T19:12:29Z. @superm1's documented subject areas include linux packaging, Docker/containers, and system info — directly relevant to a CMake build-system change for library discovery on Linux. There were no inline review comments and no requests for changes; the approval came without conditions. No reviewer had to push back or revisit scope.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change only alters how CMake locates a system library. No new network calls, credential handling, code execution paths, or permission changes. Supply-chain surface is unchanged (still the same system library, just discovered differently).
evidence.tests: No unit tests were added, which is appropriate — this is a CMake build-system change, not runtime behavior. The author reported testing on target (AMD GPU hardware): building with PKG_CONFIG_PATH set to non-standard libdrm locations, verifying linkage with ldd, testing the error condition when pkg-config cannot find the library, and running lemond on the target. CI confirms: the 'C++ Server Build, Test, and Release' workflow succeeded on Linux amd64 and arm64, 'Container Build Tests' passed on both amd64 and arm64, and all other CI check suites (MCP Smoke Test, Docs And Style, Routing Schema Tests, etc.) passed. No tests were weakened or deleted.

subject: Use pkgconfig to find libdrm_amdgpu (#3516)
summary: Switches libdrm_amdgpu discovery in CMakeLists.txt from bare library name linking to pkg-config-based detection, supporting non-standard library and include paths on Linux.
verdict_reason: A small, well-scoped build-system improvement reviewed by someone with relevant Linux packaging expertise, with CI passing across all platforms and the author confirming on-target testing.
